sanskrit: anto nūnaṃ bhavitāyaṃ kurūṇāṃ; sudāruṇaḥ sarvaharo vināśaḥ vācaḥ kāvyāḥ suhṛdāṃ pathyarūpā; na śrūyante vardhate lobha eva
english: Surely the end of the Kurus is at hand — a terrible, all-consuming destruction. The wholesome words of wise friends go unheard; only greed grows.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca dhig astu kṣattāram iti bruvāṇo; darpeṇa matto dhṛtarāṣṭrasya putraḥ avaikṣata prātikāmīṃ sabhāyām; uvāca cainaṃ paramāryamadhye
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Crying "Shame on Kṣattṛ!" and intoxicated with arrogance, the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra looked toward the Pratikamin in the assembly and spoke to him in the midst of the great nobles.

sanskrit: tvaṃ prātikāmin draupadīm ānayasva; na te bhayaṃ vidyate pāṇḍavebhyaḥ kṣattā hy ayaṃ vivadaty eva bhīrur; na cāsmākaṃ vṛddhikāmaḥ sadaiva
english: "You, Pratikamin, go and fetch Draupadī. You need have no fear of the Pāṇḍavas. This Kṣattṛ is a coward who only argues; he has never truly wished for our welfare."

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ prātikāmī sa sūtaḥ; prāyāc chīghraṃ rājavaco niśamya praviśya ca śveva sa siṃhagoṣṭhaṃ; samāsadan mahiṣīṃ pāṇḍavānām
english: Thus commanded, that charioteer Pratikamin, hearing the king's word, went quickly and entered the lion's den as a dog might, and approached the queen of the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: prātikāmy uvāca yudhiṣṭhire dyūtamadena matte; duryodhano draupadi tvām ajaiṣīt sā prapadya tvaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭrasya veśma; nayāmi tvāṃ karmaṇe yājñaseni
english: The Pratikamin said: "O Draupadī, Yudhiṣṭhira was maddened by the dice-game, and Duryodhana has won you. Therefore enter the house of Dhṛtarāṣṭra — I am taking you there to your duties, O daughter of Yajñasena."

sanskrit: draupady uvāca kathaṃ tv evaṃ vadasi prātikāmin; ko vai dīvyed bhāryayā rājaputraḥ mūḍho rājā dyūtamadena matta; āho nānyat kaitavam asya kiṃ cit
english: Draupadī said: "How do you say such a thing, Pratikamin? What prince would wager his wife at dice? Is the king truly so foolish and maddened by the game, or was there no other stake he could find?"

sanskrit: prātikāmy uvāca yadā nābhūt kaitavam anyad asya; tadādevīt pāṇḍavo 'jātaśatruḥ nyastāḥ pūrvaṃ bhrātaras tena rājñā; svayaṃ cātmā tvam atho rājaputri
english: The Pratikamin said: "When there was no other stake for him, then Yudhiṣṭhira the Pāṇḍava — the one who has no enemies — wagered. First he staked his brothers, then himself, and finally you, O princess."

sanskrit: draupady uvāca gaccha tvaṃ kitavaṃ gatvā sabhāyāṃ pṛccha sūtaja kiṃ nu pūrvaṃ parājaiṣīr ātmānaṃ māṃ nu bhārata etaj jñātvā tvam āgaccha tato māṃ naya sūtaja
english: Draupadī said: "Go, son of a charioteer — go to the gambler in the assembly and ask him this: O Bhārata, did you lose yourself first, or me? Having learned the answer, come back and then take me, O son of a charioteer."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca sabhāṃ gatvā sa covāca draupadyās tad vacas tadā kasyeśo naḥ parājaiṣīr iti tvām āha draupadī kiṃ nu pūrvaṃ parājaiṣīr ātmānam atha vāpi mām
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Going to the assembly, he conveyed Draupadī's words: "Draupadī asks you — who is the master of whom did you lose first? Did you first lose yourself, or me?"

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiras tu niśceṣṭo gatasattva ivābhavat na taṃ sūtaṃ pratyuvāca vacanaṃ sādhv asādhu vā
english: But Yudhiṣṭhira sat motionless, as if bereft of life. He gave the charioteer no reply — neither good nor ill.

sanskrit: duryodhana uvāca ihaitya kṛṣṇā pāñcālī praśnam etaṃ prabhāṣatām ihaiva sarve śṛṇvantu tasyā asya ca yad vacaḥ
english: Duryodhana said: "Let Kṛṣṇa the Pāñcālī come here herself and put her question here — let everyone hear her words and his answer."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca sa gatvā rājabhavanaṃ duryodhanavaśānugaḥ uvāca draupadīṃ sūtaḥ prātikāmī vyathann iva
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: He who followed Duryodhana's will went to the royal quarters and, as if pained, the charioteer Pratikamin spoke to Draupadī.

sanskrit: sabhyās tv amī rājaputry āhvayanti; manye prāptaḥ saṃkṣayaḥ kauravāṇām na vai samṛddhiṃ pālayate laghīyān; yat tvaṃ sabhām eṣyasi rājaputri
english: "The men of the assembly summon you, O princess. I believe the destruction of the Kauravas is at hand — for no lesser deed preserves prosperity, that you must now enter the assembly, O princess."

sanskrit: draupady uvāca evaṃ nūnaṃ vyadadhāt saṃvidhātā; sparśāv ubhau spṛśato dhīrabālau dharmaṃ tv ekaṃ paramaṃ prāha loke; sa naḥ śamaṃ dhāsyati gopyamānaḥ
english: Draupadī said: "Thus surely has the Creator ordained — that both the wise and the foolish are touched by touch alike. But there is one supreme dharma proclaimed in this world; if cherished, it will bring us peace."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca yudhiṣṭhiras tu tac chrutvā duryodhanacikīrṣitam draupadyāḥ saṃmataṃ dūtaṃ prāhiṇod bharatarṣabha
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Yudhiṣṭhira, hearing what Duryodhana intended, sent a messenger approved by Draupadī, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: ekavastrā adhonīvī rodamānā rajasvalā sabhām āgamya pāñcālī śvaśurasyāgrato 'bhavat
english: Clad in a single garment, her lower robe loose, weeping and in her monthly course, the Pāñcālī came to the assembly and stood before her father-in-law.

sanskrit: tatas teṣāṃ mukham ālokya rājā; duryodhanaḥ sūtam uvāca hṛṣṭaḥ ihaivaitām ānaya prātikāmin; pratyakṣam asyāḥ kuravo bruvantu
english: Then, looking at their faces, King Duryodhana, filled with joy, said to the charioteer: "Bring her here, Pratikamin — let the Kurus speak openly before her."

sanskrit: tataḥ sūtas tasya vaśānugāmī; bhītaś ca kopād drupadātmajāyāḥ vihāya mānaṃ punar eva sabhyān; uvāca kṛṣṇāṃ kim ahaṃ bravīmi
english: Then the charioteer, who followed his master's will but feared the wrath of the daughter of Drupada, setting aside his pride, turned to the assembly members again and said: "What shall I tell Kṛṣṇa?"

sanskrit: duryodhana uvāca duḥśāsanaiṣa mama sūtaputro; vṛkodarād udvijate 'lpacetāḥ svayaṃ pragṛhyānaya yājñasenīṃ; kiṃ te kariṣyanty avaśāḥ sapatnāḥ
english: Duryodhana said: "Duḥśāsana, this charioteer's son of mine is faint-hearted, afraid of Vṛkodara. Yourself take the daughter of Yajñasena and bring her. What can her helpless enemies do to you?"

sanskrit: tataḥ samutthāya sa rājaputraḥ; śrutvā bhrātuḥ kopaviraktadṛṣṭiḥ praviśya tad veśma mahārathānām; ity abravīd draupadīṃ rājaputrīm
english: Then that prince arose, his eyes red with rage at his brother's words, entered the dwelling of the great warriors, and spoke thus to the princess Draupadī.

sanskrit: ehy ehi pāñcāli jitāsi kṛṣṇe; duryodhanaṃ paśya vimuktalajjā kurūn bhajasvāyatapadmanetre; dharmeṇa labdhāsi sabhāṃ paraihi
english: "Come, come, Pāñcālī, O Kṛṣṇa — you have been won! Look upon Duryodhana, O lotus-eyed one, cast off your shame and join the Kurus. You have been lawfully won; go to the assembly."

sanskrit: tataḥ samutthāya sudurmanāḥ sā; vivarṇam āmṛjya mukhaṃ kareṇa ārtā pradudrāva yataḥ striyas tā; vṛddhasya rājñaḥ kurupuṃgavasya
english: Then she arose, deeply distressed, wiped her pale face with her hand, and in her affliction ran toward where the women were — the quarters of the aged king, bull of the Kurus.

sanskrit: tato javenābhisasāra roṣād; duḥśāsanas tām abhigarjamānaḥ dīrgheṣu nīleṣv atha cormimatsu; jagrāha keśeṣu narendrapatnīm
english: Then Duḥśāsana rushed after her in fury, roaring at her, and seized the wife of the king of kings by her long, dark, wavy hair.

sanskrit: ye rājasūyāvabhṛthe jalena; mahākratau mantrapūtena siktāḥ te pāṇḍavānāṃ paribhūya vīryaṃ; balāt pramṛṣṭā dhṛtarāṣṭrajena
english: Those tresses which had been drenched with the sacred waters of the Rājasūya concluding bath, at that great ceremony purified by mantras — those were now seized by force by the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, who had overcome the valor of the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: sa tāṃ parāmṛśya sabhāsamīpam; ānīya kṛṣṇām atikṛṣṇakeśīm duḥśāsano nāthavatīm anāthavac; cakarṣa vāyuḥ kadalīm ivārtām
english: Having seized her, Duḥśāsana dragged Kṛṣṇa of the very dark tresses toward the assembly — dragging her who had protectors as though she had none, as the wind drags a plantain tree in distress.

sanskrit: sā kṛṣyamāṇā namitāṅgayaṣṭiḥ; śanair uvācādya rajasvalāsmi ekaṃ ca vāso mama mandabuddhe; sabhāṃ netuṃ nārhasi mām anārya
english: As she was being dragged, her body bent, she said softly: "Today I am in my monthly course. I have but one garment, O dull-witted one; you should not take me to the assembly, O ignoble man."

sanskrit: tato 'bravīt tāṃ prasabhaṃ nigṛhya; keśeṣu kṛṣṇeṣu tadā sa kṛṣṇām kṛṣṇaṃ ca jiṣṇuṃ ca hariṃ naraṃ ca; trāṇāya vikrośa nayāmi hi tvām
english: Then, forcibly seizing her by her dark hair, he said to Kṛṣṇa: "Cry out for protection to Kṛṣṇa, to Jiṣṇu, to Hari, to Nara — I am taking you regardless."

sanskrit: rajasvalā vā bhava yājñaseni; ekāmbarā vāpy atha vā vivastrā dyūte jitā cāsi kṛtāsi dāsī; dāsīṣu kāmaś ca yathopajoṣam
english: "Whether you are in your monthly course, O Yājñasenī, whether you wear one garment or none — you have been won at dice; you are made a slave. Among the slave women you shall serve according to desire."

sanskrit: prakīrṇakeśī patitārdhavastrā; duḥśāsanena vyavadhūyamānā hrīmaty amarṣeṇa ca dahyamānā; śanair idaṃ vākyam uvāca kṛṣṇā
english: With her hair disheveled, her half-garment fallen, being shaken about by Duḥśāsana, burning with shame and indignation, Kṛṣṇa softly spoke these words.

sanskrit: ime sabhāyām upadiṣṭaśāstrāḥ; kriyāvantaḥ sarva evendrakalpāḥ gurusthānā guravaś caiva sarve; teṣām agre notsahe sthātum evam
english: "These men in the assembly are learned in scripture, all of them active and equal to Indra; all are elders, worthy of veneration as gurus. Before them I cannot bear to stand in this state."

sanskrit: nṛśaṃsakarmaṃs tvam anāryavṛtta; mā māṃ vivastrāṃ kṛdhi mā vikārṣīḥ na marṣayeyus tava rājaputrāḥ; sendrāpi devā yadi te sahāyāḥ
english: "O doer of cruel deeds, you of ignoble conduct — do not strip me bare, do not drag me! Your royal enemies would not endure this — not even if all the gods with Indra were your allies."

sanskrit: dharme sthito dharmasutaś ca rājā; dharmaś ca sūkṣmo nipuṇopalabhyaḥ vācāpi bhartuḥ paramāṇumātraṃ; necchāmi doṣaṃ svaguṇān visṛjya
english: "The king who is the son of Dharma stands firm in righteousness. And dharma is subtle, discerned only by the wise. I do not wish to cause even an atom of fault to my husband, abandoning my own virtues even in word."

sanskrit: idaṃ tv anāryaṃ kuruvīramadhye; rajasvalāṃ yat parikarṣase mām na cāpi kaś cit kurute 'tra pūjāṃ; dhruvaṃ tavedaṃ matam anvapadyan
english: "But this is ignoble — that you drag me, in my monthly course, in the midst of Kuru heroes, and none here does me honor. Surely all these have followed your thinking."

sanskrit: dhig astu naṣṭaḥ khalu bhāratānāṃ; dharmas tathā kṣatravidāṃ ca vṛttam yatrābhyatītāṃ kurudharmavelāṃ; prekṣanti sarve kuravaḥ sabhāyām
english: "Shame! The dharma of the Bhāratas is truly lost, and so too the conduct of those who know the warrior code — for the Kurus all sit in the assembly and watch as the bounds of Kuru righteousness are transgressed."

sanskrit: droṇasya bhīṣmasya ca nāsti sattvaṃ; dhruvaṃ tathaivāsya mahātmano 'pi rājñas tathā hīmam adharmam ugraṃ; na lakṣayante kuruvṛddhamukhyāḥ
english: "There is no firmness in Droṇa, nor in Bhīṣma, nor surely in that great-souled king either — for the foremost elders of the Kurus do not mark this terrible adharma."

sanskrit: tathā bruvantī karuṇaṃ sumadhyamā; kākṣeṇa bhartṝn kupitān apaśyat sā pāṇḍavān kopaparītadehān; saṃdīpayām āsa kaṭākṣapātaiḥ
english: As she spoke thus pitifully, the slender-waisted one glanced sideways and saw her husbands overcome with rage — the Pāṇḍavas with bodies consumed by anger — and inflamed them further with the glances of her eyes.

sanskrit: hṛtena rājyena tathā dhanena; ratnaiś ca mukhyair na tathā babhūva yathārtayā kopasamīritena; kṛṣṇākaṭākṣeṇa babhūva duḥkham
english: The pain caused by the loss of their kingdom, their wealth, and their finest jewels was not as great as the pain caused by Kṛṣṇa's sidelong glance charged with anguish and fury.

sanskrit: duḥśāsanaś cāpi samīkṣya kṛṣṇām; avekṣamāṇāṃ kṛpaṇān patīṃs tān ādhūya vegena visaṃjñakalpām; uvāca dāsīti hasann ivograḥ
english: And Duḥśāsana, seeing Kṛṣṇa look piteously at those wretched husbands, shook her violently as if to render her unconscious, and said with a cruel laugh: "A slave woman!"

sanskrit: karṇas tu tad vākyam atīva hṛṣṭaḥ; saṃpūjayām āsa hasan saśabdam gāndhārarājaḥ subalasya putras; tathaiva duḥśāsanam abhyanandat
english: Karṇa was exceedingly delighted at that word and applauded it with a loud laugh. The king of Gāndhāra, son of Subala, likewise praised Duḥśāsana.

sanskrit: sabhyās tu ye tatra babhūvur anye; tābhyām ṛte dhārtarāṣṭreṇa caiva teṣām abhūd duḥkham atīva kṛṣṇāṃ; dṛṣṭvā sabhāyāṃ parikṛṣyamāṇām
english: But all the other members of the assembly who were there — excepting those two and the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra — felt extreme sorrow upon seeing Kṛṣṇa being dragged about in the assembly.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca na dharmasaukṣmyāt subhage vivaktuṃ; śaknomi te praśnam imaṃ yathāvat asvo hy aśaktaḥ paṇituṃ parasvaṃ; striyaś ca bhartur vaśatāṃ samīkṣya
english: Bhīṣma said: "O fortunate one, I am not able to answer your question properly on account of the subtlety of dharma. One who owns nothing cannot stake another's property — and women are subject to their husband's authority."

sanskrit: tyajeta sarvāṃ pṛthivīṃ samṛddhāṃ; yudhiṣṭhiraḥ satyam atho na jahyāt uktaṃ jito 'smīti ca pāṇḍavena; tasmān na śaknomi vivektum etat
english: "Yudhiṣṭhira would abandon the entire prosperous earth, but he would not abandon truth. And the Pāṇḍava has declared 'I am defeated' — therefore I cannot resolve this matter."

sanskrit: dyūte 'dvitīyaḥ śakunir nareṣu; kuntīsutas tena nisṛṣṭakāmaḥ na manyate tāṃ nikṛtiṃ mahātmā; tasmān na te praśnam imaṃ bravīmi
english: "Śakuni is unequalled among men at dice; invited by him, the son of Kuntī freely submitted to his desire. That great soul does not regard it as deception — therefore I cannot answer your question."

sanskrit: draupady uvāca āhūya rājā kuśalaiḥ sabhāyāṃ; duṣṭātmabhir naikṛtikair anāryaiḥ dyūtapriyair nātikṛtaprayatnaḥ; kasmād ayaṃ nāma nisṛṣṭakāmaḥ
english: Draupadī said: "The king was summoned to the assembly by those skilled in trickery — by evil-souled, deceitful, ignoble gamblers — with no great effort on their part. How then is he said to have freely submitted his will?"

sanskrit: sa śuddhabhāvo nikṛtipravṛttim; abudhyamānaḥ kurupāṇḍavāgryaḥ saṃbhūya sarvaiś ca jito 'pi yasmāt; paścāc ca yat kaitavam abhyupetaḥ
english: "He who is the foremost of the Kuru Pāṇḍavas — pure of heart, not perceiving the deceitful conduct — was overcome by all of them together, and it was only afterward that he accepted the terms of the gambling."

sanskrit: tiṣṭhanti ceme kuravaḥ sabhāyām; īśāḥ sutānāṃ ca tathā snuṣāṇām samīkṣya sarve mama cāpi vākyaṃ; vibrūta me praśnam imaṃ yathāvat
english: "These Kurus stand in the assembly — masters of sons and daughters-in-law alike. Let them all weigh my words as well. Answer my question truthfully, O kings."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tathā bruvantīṃ karuṇaṃ rudantīm; avekṣamāṇām asakṛt patīṃs tān duḥśāsanaḥ paruṣāṇy apriyāṇi; vākyāny uvācāmadhurāṇi caiva
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: As she spoke thus piteously and wept, repeatedly glancing at those husbands, Duḥśāsana spoke harsh, unpleasant, and bitter words to her.

sanskrit: tāṃ kṛṣyamāṇāṃ ca rajasvalāṃ ca; srastottarīyām atadarhamāṇām vṛkodaraḥ prekṣya yudhiṣṭhiraṃ ca; cakāra kopaṃ paramārtarūpaḥ
english: Seeing her being dragged, in her monthly course, her upper garment slipping, trembling — and seeing Yudhiṣṭhira — Vṛkodara, his form the very image of extreme anguish, gave vent to his rage.

sanskrit: bhīma uvāca bhavanti deśe bandhakyaḥ kitavānāṃ yudhiṣṭhira na tābhir uta dīvyanti dayā caivāsti tāsv api
english: Bhīma said: "Gamblers keep women of ill repute in their homes, O Yudhiṣṭhira — they do not even wager those, and even for those women there is compassion."

sanskrit: kāśyo yad balim āhārṣīd dravyaṃ yac cānyad uttamam tathānye pṛthivīpālā yāni ratnāny upāharan
english: "The tribute that the king of Kāśi brought, the other finest goods, and whatever jewels the other kings of the earth had offered —"

sanskrit: vāhanāni dhanaṃ caiva kavacāny āyudhāni ca rājyam ātmā vayaṃ caiva kaitavena hṛtaṃ paraiḥ
english: "— our vehicles, our wealth, our armor and weapons, our kingdom, our very selves and we ourselves — all were taken from us by the deceit of our enemies."

sanskrit: na ca me tatra kopo 'bhūt sarvasyeśo hi no bhavān idaṃ tv atikṛtaṃ manye draupadī yatra paṇyate
english: "And I felt no anger in all of that, for you are the master of all that is ours. But I consider this to be going too far — that Draupadī was staked."

sanskrit: eṣā hy anarhatī bālā pāṇḍavān prāpya kauravaiḥ tvatkṛte kliśyate kṣudrair nṛśaṃsair nikṛtipriyaiḥ
english: "This innocent girl, who did not deserve this fate, having come to the Pāṇḍavas, is now being tormented on your account by these petty, cruel, and deceit-loving Kauravas."

sanskrit: asyāḥ kṛte manyur ayaṃ tvayi rājan nipātyate bāhū te saṃpradhakṣyāmi sahadevāgnim ānaya
english: "This wrath is brought down upon you for her sake, O king. I will burn your arms to ashes — Sahadeva, bring fire!"

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca na purā bhīmasena tvam īdṛśīr vaditā giraḥ parais te nāśitaṃ nūnaṃ nṛśaṃsair dharmagauravam
english: Arjuna said: "You have never before, O Bhīmasena, spoken such words. Surely the respect for dharma in you has been destroyed by these cruel enemies."

sanskrit: na sakāmāḥ pare kāryā dharmam evācarottamam bhrātaraṃ dhārmikaṃ jyeṣṭhaṃ nātikramitum arhati
english: "Our enemies must not be made to rejoice. Practice only the highest dharma. One should not transgress the eldest brother who is righteous."

sanskrit: āhūto hi parai rājā kṣātradharmam anusmaran dīvyate parakāmena tan naḥ kīrtikaraṃ mahat
english: "The king, summoned by enemies, plays at dice keeping in mind the warrior's dharma, submitting to another's will — this is greatly glorious for us."

sanskrit: bhīmasena uvāca evam asmikṛtaṃ vidyāṃ yady asyāhaṃ dhanaṃjaya dīpte 'gnau sahitau bāhū nirdaheyaṃ balād iva
english: Bhīmasena said: "Had I known this was being done to me, O Dhanañjaya, I would have burned both his arms in a blazing fire, as if by force."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tathā tān duḥkhitān dṛṣṭvā pāṇḍavān dhṛtarāṣṭrajaḥ kliśyamānāṃ ca pāñcālīṃ vikarṇa idam abravīt
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Seeing the Pāṇḍavas in such distress, and the Pāñcālī being tormented, Vikarṇa, the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, spoke these words.

sanskrit: yājñasenyā yad uktaṃ tad vākyaṃ vibrūta pārthivāḥ avivekena vākyasya narakaḥ sadya eva naḥ
english: "Answer the words spoken by the daughter of Yajñasena, O kings. By not discerning the truth of her words, we will immediately fall into hell."

sanskrit: bhīṣmaś ca dhṛtarāṣṭraś ca kuruvṛddhatamāv ubhau sametya nāhatuḥ kiṃ cid viduraś ca mahāmatiḥ
english: "Both Bhīṣma and Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the two eldest of the Kurus, have said nothing after coming together here, nor has the great-minded Vidura."

sanskrit: bhāradvājo 'pi sarveṣām ācāryaḥ kṛpa eva ca ata etāv api praśnaṃ nāhatur dvijasattamau
english: "And the son of Bharadvaja, who is the preceptor of all, and Kṛpa — even these two foremost of the twice-born have not answered the question."

sanskrit: ye tv anye pṛthivīpālāḥ sametāḥ sarvato diśaḥ kāmakrodhau samutsṛjya te bruvantu yathāmati
english: "But those other kings of the earth who have assembled here from all directions — setting aside desire and anger, let them speak according to their understanding."

sanskrit: yad idaṃ draupadī vākyam uktavaty asakṛc chubhā vimṛśya kasya kaḥ pakṣaḥ pārthivā vadatottaram
english: "This word that auspicious Draupadī has repeatedly uttered — reflecting carefully, whose side is which? O kings, speak your reply."

sanskrit: evaṃ sa bahuśaḥ sarvān uktavāṃs tān sabhāsadaḥ na ca te pṛthivīpālās tam ūcuḥ sādhv asādhu vā
english: Thus he repeatedly addressed all the members of the assembly, yet those kings of the earth said nothing to him — neither good nor ill.

sanskrit: uktvā tathāsakṛt sarvān vikarṇaḥ pṛthivīpatīn pāṇiṃ pāṇau viniṣpiṣya niḥśvasann idam abravīt
english: Having thus repeatedly addressed all the kings, Vikarṇa rubbed one palm against the other, and sighing, spoke these words.

sanskrit: vibrūta pṛthivīpālā vākyaṃ mā vā kathaṃ cana manye nyāyyaṃ yad atrāhaṃ tad dhi vakṣyāmi kauravāḥ
english: "Speak, O kings, or speak not at all. What I consider to be just here, that I shall proclaim, O Kauravas."

sanskrit: catvāry āhur naraśreṣṭhā vyasanāni mahīkṣitām mṛgayāṃ pānam akṣāṃś ca grāmye caivātisaktatām
english: "The foremost men declare four vices of kings: hunting, drinking, gambling, and excessive attachment to sensual pleasures."

sanskrit: eteṣu hi naraḥ sakto dharmam utsṛjya vartate tathāyuktena ca kṛtāṃ kriyāṃ loko na manyate
english: "A man addicted to these lives having abandoned dharma, and the world does not regard an act done by one thus afflicted as valid."

sanskrit: tad ayaṃ pāṇḍuputreṇa vyasane vartatā bhṛśam samāhūtena kitavair āsthito draupadīpaṇaḥ
english: "This son of Pāṇḍu, deeply caught in vice, summoned by gamblers, staked Draupadī as a wager."

sanskrit: sādhāraṇī ca sarveṣāṃ pāṇḍavānām aninditā jitena pūrvaṃ cānena pāṇḍavena kṛtaḥ paṇaḥ
english: "Moreover, she is the common wife of all the Pāṇḍavas, the irreproachable one. And the stake was made by this Pāṇḍava after he had already been won himself."

sanskrit: iyaṃ ca kīrtitā kṛṣṇā saubalena paṇārthinā etat sarvaṃ vicāryāhaṃ manye na vijitām imām
english: "And this Kṛṣṇa was named as a stake by Subala's son who desired to win. Considering all of this, I believe she has not been won."

sanskrit: etac chrutvā mahān nādaḥ sabhyānām udatiṣṭhata vikarṇaṃ śaṃsamānānāṃ saubalaṃ ca vinindatām
english: Hearing this, a great roar arose from the members of the assembly — some praising Vikarṇa and condemning the son of Subala.

sanskrit: tasminn uparate śabde rādheyaḥ krodhamūrchitaḥ pragṛhya ruciraṃ bāhum idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: When that noise subsided, the son of Rādhā, nearly fainting with rage, lifted his beautiful arm and spoke these words.

sanskrit: dṛśyante vai vikarṇe hi vaikṛtāni bahūny api tajjas tasya vināśāya yathāgnir araṇiprajaḥ
english: "Many perversities are indeed visible in Vikarṇa. The fire born of the fire-sticks leads to the destruction of those very sticks — so too with him."

sanskrit: ete na kiṃ cid apy āhuś codyamānāpi kṛṣṇayā dharmeṇa vijitāṃ manye manyante drupadātmajām
english: "All these have said nothing even when urged by Kṛṣṇa herself. I consider the daughter of Drupada to have been won by dharma — they too think so."

sanskrit: tvaṃ tu kevalabālyena dhārtarāṣṭra vidīryase yad bravīṣi sabhāmadhye bālaḥ sthavirabhāṣitam
english: "But you, O son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, are bursting with sheer childishness — speaking in the assembly like a child trying to sound like an elder."

sanskrit: na ca dharmaṃ yathātattvaṃ vetsi duryodhanāvara yad bravīṣi jitāṃ kṛṣṇām ajiteti sumandadhīḥ
english: "And you do not know dharma as it truly is, O lesser one to Duryodhana — you of very dull wit who proclaims the won Kṛṣṇa to be unwon."

sanskrit: kathaṃ hy avijitāṃ kṛṣṇāṃ manyase dhṛtarāṣṭraja yadā sabhāyāṃ sarvasvaṃ nyastavān pāṇḍavāgrajaḥ
english: "How can you consider Kṛṣṇa to be unwon, O son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, when the eldest of the Pāṇḍavas staked his entire self in the assembly?"

sanskrit: abhyantarā ca sarvasve draupadī bharatarṣabha evaṃ dharmajitāṃ kṛṣṇāṃ manyase na jitāṃ katham
english: "And Draupadī is included within 'all that he possesses,' O bull of the Bhāratas. How then do you consider Kṛṣṇa, won by dharma, to be unwon?"
